data.title: Log Analyst
data.findings: Root cause: DB connection pool exhaustion in payment-service, not a payment-gateway/provider problem. Deploy dep-4821 rolled out at 21:37:42 (3/3 pods); at 21:38:42 the DB pool saturated to 5/5 (max size 5 — unusually small) and connection acquisition began timing out after 5000ms, producing cascading 'PoolTimeoutError: could not acquire connection within 5000ms' charge failures (ord-88159, ord-88171, ord-88204, etc.) and a healthcheck alert 'db pool saturation 100%' at 21:45:42. No gateway-specific errors were seen — the one successful charge logged (21:16:42, gw=razorpay, 210ms) predates the deploy, and no razorpay/gateway timeout or cert-expiry errors appear in the logs. grep for 'dep-4821' shows the deploy event only in payments logs, indicating this is a payments-service-local, single-deploy-triggered issue (likely pool size misconfigured or connections not released in dep-4821) rather than a global/multi-region or upstream-gateway failure; the elevated error rates in api-gateway (14.2%) and orders (22.4%) are downstream cascades of payments' failures, not independent root causes. Recommend: roll back dep-4821 and/or increase DB pool size, and audit dep-4821's diff for connection-handling changes (e.g., missing connection release, new query holding locks longer).

data.thought: Root cause identified as DB pool exhaustion from dep-4821; next need a concrete fix proposal (rollback and/or pool size increase) for human approval.

data.title: Fix Engineer
data.objective: INC-2041 root cause: deploy dep-4821 (rolled out 21:37:42) caused DB connection pool exhaustion in payment-service (pool max size only 5, saturated to 5/5 at 21:38:42), producing cascading PoolTimeoutError failures on charge attempts and 214 orders stuck in PENDING_PAYMENT. Propose a concrete remediation plan: (1) immediate mitigation — rollback dep-4821 to last known-good version and/or hotfix increasing DB pool size to a safe value, (2) steps to safely reprocess/reconcile the 214 PENDING_PAYMENT orders (avoid double-charging), (3) audit dep-4821's diff for connection leak (e.g. missing connection release/unclosed transactions), (4) verification steps to confirm error rate returns below 5% threshold post-fix. Flag clearly that rollback/deploy actions require human approval before execution.

data.findings: Root cause confirmed via get_recent_deploys: dep-4821 (payments, priya.k, 2026-08-24 21:37:42) dropped DB_POOL_SIZE from 50 to 5 while also bumping PG_DRIVER 8.11->8.12, matching the pool-exhaustion signature (5/5 saturated at 21:38:42). (1) Immediate mitigation: patch-1 proposed via propose_patch — restore DB_POOL_SIZE to 50 in payments config; currently status=awaiting_approval, NOT applied — requires human sign-off before apply. Recommend commander also consider a full rollback of dep-4821 to the pre-8.12 driver version as a parallel/backup option if the pool-size hotfix alone doesn't resolve saturation, since the driver bump is unverified as safe. (2) Reconciliation of 214 PENDING_PAYMENT orders: once pool capacity is restored and error rate confirmed stable, reprocess orders via idempotency-key-guarded retry (do not blind-retry charges) — query payment gateway/PSP for existing charge status per order id before re-attempting, mark orders with a found successful charge as PAID without recharging, and only submit fresh charge attempts for orders with no matching gateway record; this avoids double-charging. (3) Diff audit: I only have the config diff (pool size, driver version) from get_recent_deploys, not code-level diff — flag to engineering to pull the actual code diff for dep-4821 to check for missing connection.release()/unclosed transactions introduced by the pg driver 8.11->8.12 bump, since the config change alone (50->5) is sufficient to explain exhaustion but a leak would explain why even 5 connections saturated so fast. (4) Verification: after human-approves and applies the pool-size hotfix (and/or rollback), monitor payment-service error rate and DB pool utilization for 15-30 min, confirm error rate <5% and pool utilization stays below max sustained, then close incident; keep patch-1 and any rollback action gated on explicit human approval per policy.

data.text:
UPDATE 1 — Investigating (2026-08-24, ~22:00 UTC)

We're aware that some customers experienced failed or stuck payments during checkout starting at 21:38 UTC today. If you tried to complete a purchase and it didn't go through, your order may currently show as pending — please don't attempt to pay again, as we are making sure no one is charged twice.

What we know: our team traced the issue to a configuration change from a recent deployment that reduced database capacity for payment processing. A fix has been prepared and is going through final validation before we roll it out, to make sure it fully resolves the issue without side effects.

What this means for you: no action is needed on your part. Any order affected by this issue will be reviewed and reconciled once the fix is in place, and you will not be double-charged.

Next update: within 60 minutes, or sooner if the fix is deployed.

---

UPDATE 2 — Resolved (to send once patch is approved and applied)

This issue is now resolved. The configuration fix has been validated and rolled out, and checkout is processing payments normally again.

We've reviewed the orders affected by this outage and reconciled them — no customer was charged more than once. If your order was stuck as pending, it has now been corrected, and you should see the accurate status reflected in your account. If you paid and still don't see confirmation, or notice anything unexpected on your statement, please contact support and we'll take care of it right away.

We're sorry for the disruption this caused during your checkout experience, and thank you for your patience while we fixed it.

data.summary: INC-2041 (2026-08-24 21:38:42): Payment-service error rate spiked to 61.7% (threshold 5%), collapsing checkout conversion and leaving 214 orders in PENDING_PAYMENT. Root cause: deploy dep-4821 (priya.k, 21:37:42) dropped DB_POOL_SIZE from 50 to 5 (alongside an unverified pg driver bump 8.11->8.12), saturating the payment-service DB pool by 21:38:42 and causing cascading PoolTimeoutError charge failures; downstream error rates in api-gateway (14.2%) and orders (22.4%) were cascades, not independent causes. Fix: patch-1 (restore DB_POOL_SIZE to 50) proposed by fix_engineer, status=awaiting_approval — requires human sign-off before apply; full rollback of dep-4821 held as backup if pool-size fix alone is insufficient, and engineering should still pull the code-level diff to rule out a connection leak from the driver bump. Reconciliation plan for the 214 stuck orders: query PSP for existing charge status per order before any retry, mark orders with a confirmed charge as PAID without recharging, only submit fresh charges for orders with no gateway record — avoiding double-charging. Comms: 'Investigating' status-page update drafted (advises customers not to retry payment, discloses config-change root cause, promises reconciliation) and a 'Resolved' version is queued to publish once the patch is approved and deployed and error rate is confirmed <5% for 15-30 min. Follow-ups: (1) human approval + deploy of patch-1, (2) post-fix monitoring of error rate and pool utilization, (3) code-diff audit of dep-4821 for connection leaks, (4) reconcile and clear the 214 PENDING_PAYMENT orders, (5) publish Resolved comms once verified.
